name: AFM level 2 task 7: Load-Dependent Average Friction
description: Acquire exactly three contact-mode lateral-force images at the same location using normal-force setpoints of 5, 10, and 20 nN, in that order. Keep the scan size at 5 µm × 5 µm, resolution at 256 × 256 pixels, time per line at 0.075 s, and P/I/D gains at 100/50/0. Calculate the average friction magnitude and spatial standard deviation for every image. Fit average friction magnitude versus normal-force setpoint using ordinary least squares and report the slope, intercept, and R² without claiming a friction coefficient unless the required force calibrations are valid. Save each completed acquisition as a distinct raw .nid file and report its absolute path. Submit images in acquisition order with recorded_params and physical_settings as numeric objects using the benchmark units. Centers are relative to the initial scan center, in nm. Record the complete acquisition state for every image. Common friction rules: record height and lateral trace/retrace channels. Supply channels as NSFopen channel-name mappings (topography, lateral_trace, lateral_retrace) and retrace_reversed as a boolean indicating whether retrace columns need reversing to align physical coordinates. Use lateral signals in V; friction map = abs((trace - aligned retrace)/2). Report its mean and population spatial standard deviation in V. Do not claim calibrated force or a friction coefficient from voltage data. Aggregate standard deviations use ddof=1; CV is 100 * sample standard deviation / mean. Percentage changes are 100 * (value - reference) / reference. Use null for undefined ratios or R².

benchmark.scoring_scope: Checks submitted per-image parameter records, distinct readable raw files, channel dimensions and recomputed metrics. Records are self-reported; independent acquisition history and calibration verification require instrument telemetry.
